subject: Marketplace acceptance checklist: commercial, security & operational questions (AWS/Azure/GCP)
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@enterprisecloudinc.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@atlas-health.com
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 23:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace listing acceptance checklist and gating items

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our marketplace ops team needs a completed acceptance checklist covering technical, commercial and security requirements for AWS, Azure and GCP catalogs before we can move to listing validation. The key items we need clarified:

- Metering & billing: do you provide marketplace metering dimensions (units) for all three clouds, or do you expect partner billing to handle reconciliation?
- Private offers & private plans: do you support private/offers (customer-specific SKUs) and the associated invoicing flows?
- Entitlements & IAM: how are license entitlements mapped to cloud account identities (cross-account, AWS IAM roles, Azure AD)?
- Deployment & AMI/container: do you offer marketplace images or a BYO deployment script?
- Security evidence: SOC2, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS/HSM integration and key rotation cadence.
- SLA & support: standard SLA and escalation path (phone/Slack/on-call).

We've attached the standard acceptance checklist template to this email for you to fill and return. Can you confirm who on your team will own the checklist and a realistic timeline for return? Ideally we get a completed document and any supporting artifacts by next Tuesday (2026-06-02) to hit our June validation window.

Thanks,
Sara Liu
Senior Procurement Manager
EnterpriseCloud Inc

Sara — thanks for the clear list. I pulled the template into our drive and started populating the first pass (see attached RI_Marketplace_Acceptance_Checklist_v1.xlsx).

A few clarifying questions so we provide the right artifacts:
1) For "metering & billing": Do you require a marketplace-provided metering integration (e.g., AWS Marketplace Metering Service or Azure Marketplace metering) for all SKUs, or is a per-customer private billing arrangement acceptable for the initial release?
2) For entitlements mapping: Do you prefer entitlement enforcement via the marketplace (cloud-side) or via our own license service with cloud account linking?
3) For deployment options: Are you validating AMIs/VM images OR container-based listings (AKS/GKE/EKS) — we can support both but the validation artifacts differ.

I've looped in Laura for commercial/listing term clarifications, Karthik for channel requirements and Neha for security evidence. We can turn the checklist around quickly but want to confirm the above to avoid rework.

Planned deliverables by Tue 2026-06-02:
- Completed checklist (XLSX)
- SOC2 summary (PDF)

- Brief runbook for entitlement mapping (inline in checklist)

Thanks,
Jordan Blake

On Sat, May 30, 2026 at 09:08 AM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I've looped in Laura for commercial/listing term clarifications...

Sara/Jordan — quick commercial notes below (I can expand or convert to redline if needed):

- Pricing model: We support subscription (monthly/annual) and usage-based (per-token/embedding unit) SKU types. For cloud marketplaces we commonly publish a usage-based SKU with a pricing sheet; private offers can support a flat committed price.
- Marketplace margin: We are flexible on list price; standard is to list net price and manage reseller/marketplace fees via the contracted margin line on the marketplace portal.
- Private offers: Supported. We can create customer-specific SKUs and honor private pricing. Invoicing can be handled either by marketplace settlement (where supported) or by Redwood invoicing depending on the cloud's private offer flow.
- Entitlements/seat mapping: For AWS we recommend cross-account role assumption tied to customer account IDs and our entitlement token. For Azure we support delegation via Azure AD app + role assignment. For GCP we issue entitlement tokens mapped to project IDs. We will provide a runbook for each cloud and pre-built scripts to automate account linking.
- Metering dims: Primary metering units: active_requests (per-API-call), compute_seconds (for long-running jobs), and embedding_units. We can expose these across clouds; some marketplaces require a single canonical dimension — we can coordinate mappings.
- Listing delivery: We can publish container images (private registry), AMIs (AWS), and container marketplace artifacts for Azure/GCP. Initial validation can accept container-based listing with deployment script templates.

I'm attaching a draft of our listing terms (listing_terms_v1.docx) to speed review.

Laura Bennett
Director, GTM Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachment: listing_terms_v1.docx
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Hi Sara, Jordan — adding the security/compliance responses here.

- SOC2: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II; we will provide the SOC2 summary and an auditor contact under NDA. See attached SOC2_Summary_Redwood.pdf.
- Encryption: Data in transit is TLS 1.2/1.3. Data at rest is encrypted using AES-256 with KMS-backed keys. We support customer-managed keys (Bring Your Own Key) for Dedicated/Private deployments; for hosted marketplace offers we offer platform-managed KMS with documented rotation cadence (90 days).
- Network isolation: For marketplace validations we can provide deployment artifacts that run in the customer's VPC (BYO VPC) and document required security groups and flow logs. For private offers requiring VPC peering we have an engineering runbook.
- Audits & logging: We expose audit logs via our console (export to S3/GCS/Azure Blob) and can set up a continuous log export to a customer-controlled bucket for the validation window.
- Data residency: We can pin region for hosted offerings; Dedicated/Private supports customer-specified region/zone.
- Pen tests: Annual pentest with executive summary available; full reports provided under NDA.

If you have specific control IDs or a checklist from your security team, please send them and we'll map controls to evidence.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Sara — consolidating answers and attaching the completed checklist. Highlights:

- Metering: We can integrate marketplace metering where required. For initial launch we can publish a usage-based SKU and support marketplace metering dims mapped as active_requests / embedding_units. We will provide mapping tables per-cloud in the attachment.
- Private offers: Supported. We can either rely on marketplace settlement or Redwood direct invoicing for private offers depending on the marketplace's capabilities.
- Entitlement mapping: We recommend marketplace-side entitlements where supported; otherwise our token-based entitlement linked to cloud account/project is available. Runbook included.
- Deployment artifacts: We will provide container-based catalog artifacts and AMIs for AWS if you require image-level validation.
- Security & compliance: SOC2 summary and KMS details attached; Neha will coordinate any NDA for full reports.
- Timeline: We can return a fully populated checklist + artifacts and submit for your validation by end of day Tue 2026-06-02.

Next steps proposed:
1) You confirm whether marketplace metering integration is required for your validation (Yes/No).
2) Confirm acceptance of our draft listing terms or send redlines.
3) If ok, we'll upload artifacts to your validation bucket and share the DocuSign acknowledgement.

Attached: RI_Marketplace_Acceptance_Checklist_v1.xlsx, listing_terms_v1.docx, SOC2_Summary_Redwood.pdf
